meaning: Of all the A, B is the most …. Names a group of three or more and picks the top one; also the shape of the question 〜の中で何が一番〜ですか.

examples.ja: {果物|くだもの}の{中|なか}でりんごが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Of all fruits, I like apples best.

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}[[の{中|なか}で]]{父|ちち}が{一番|いちばん}{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My father is the tallest in my family.

examples.ja: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}の{中|なか}で{何曜日|なんようび}[[が]]{一番|いちばん}{忙|いそが}しいですか。
examples.en: Which day of the week are you busiest?

questions.ja: {動物|どうぶつ}の{中|なか}[[で]]{犬|いぬ}が{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きです。
questions.en: Of all animals, I like dogs best.
questions.explain: の中で sets the group you are choosing from; に, を and へ can't do that.

questions.ja: この{三|みっ}つの{中|なか}で、どれが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{安|やす}いですか。
questions.en: Of these three, which one is the cheapest?
questions.explain: Picking the top one out of three or more takes 一番.

meaning: Because / so. Gives a reason in a soft, explanatory way, which suits requests and apologies. After a noun or な-adjective it becomes なので.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている[[ので]]、{今日|きょう}は{出|で}かけません。
examples.en: It's raining, so I'm not going out today.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みな[[ので]]、ゆっくり{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: Tomorrow is my day off, so I'll sleep in.

examples.ja: {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い[[ので]]、{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}ってもいいですか。
examples.en: I have a headache, so may I go home early?

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}かな[[ので]]、よく{勉強|べんきょう}できます。
examples.en: This room is quiet, so I can study well here.

questions.ja: {風邪|かぜ}をひいた[[ので]]、{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}みます。
questions.en: I've caught a cold, so I'm staying home from school.
questions.explain: The cold is the reason for staying home, so the link is ので, not a contrast.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}[[なので]]、{銀行|ぎんこう}は{休|やす}みです。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, so the bank is closed.
questions.explain: After a noun, ので becomes なので; なのに would mean 'even though'.

meaning: Polite prefixes for nouns. お goes on most native Japanese words (お茶, お金) and ご on most Chinese-origin words (ご家族, ご両親); some words almost always carry one.

examples.ja: [[お]]{茶|ちゃ}をどうぞ。
examples.en: Please have some tea.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}の[[ご]]{家族|かぞく}は{何人|なんにん}ですか。
examples.en: How many people are there in your teacher's family?

examples.ja: [[お]]{名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.en: What is your name?

examples.ja: もう[[ご]]{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましたか。
examples.en: Have you eaten yet?

questions.ja: すみません、[[お]]{手洗|てあら}いはどこですか。
questions.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
questions.explain: 手洗い is a native word and the polite form is always お手洗い.

questions.ja: {山下|やました}さんの[[ご]]{両親|りょうしん}はお{元気|げんき}ですか。
questions.en: Are Yamashita-san's parents well?
questions.explain: 両親 is a Chinese-origin word, so it takes ご.

meaning: Marks the direct object, the thing an action is done to. With movement verbs it also marks the place you pass through or leave (道を歩く, 家を出る).

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、コーヒー[[を]]{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}で{本|ほん}[[を]]{借|か}りました。
examples.en: I borrowed a book at the library.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}[[を]]まっすぐ{歩|ある}いてください。
examples.en: Please walk straight along this road.

examples.ja: {八時|はちじ}に{家|いえ}[[を]]{出|で}ます。
examples.en: I leave home at eight.

questions.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}、{日本語|にほんご}の{新聞|しんぶん}[[を]]{読|よ}みます。
questions.en: Every evening I read a Japanese newspaper.
questions.explain: The newspaper is what gets read, so it is the object and takes を.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}[[を]]{降|お}りました。
questions.en: I got off the train at the station.
questions.explain: 降りる marks the thing you get off with を; に goes with 乗る.

meaning: Please give me N. The everyday way to ask for or order something; a quantity goes after を: 水を二つください.

examples.ja: すみません、{水|みず}[[をください]]。
examples.en: Excuse me, some water, please.

examples.ja: このりんごを{三|みっ}つ[[ください]]。
examples.en: Three of these apples, please.

examples.ja: その{赤|あか}いかばん[[をください]]。
examples.en: I'll take that red bag, please.

questions.ja: あの{白|しろ}いシャツ[[を]]ください。
questions.en: That white shirt, please.
questions.explain: The thing you ask for is the object of ください, so it takes を.

questions.ja: {切手|きって}を{三枚|さんまい}[[ください]]。
questions.en: Three stamps, please.
questions.explain: Noun + を + amount + ください asks for things; を comes once, before the amount, and てください follows a verb.

meaning: However. Opens a sentence that goes against the one before it. Formal and mostly written; in conversation でも is more usual.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いです。[[しかし]]、あまりおいしくないです。
examples.en: This place is cheap. However, the food isn't very good.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです。[[しかし]]、とても{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Japanese is difficult. However, it's very interesting.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しました。[[しかし]]、テストはよくできませんでした。
examples.en: I practised every day. However, the test went badly.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}みました。[[しかし]]、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I took some medicine. However, my head still hurts.
questions.explain: The headache continuing goes against what you'd expect, so a contrast word is needed.

questions.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きです。[[しかし]]、あまり{上手|じょうず}じゃありません。
questions.en: Yamashita-san likes cooking. However, she isn't very good at it.
questions.explain: Liking it but not being good at it is a contrast, which しかし introduces.

meaning: And then / after that. Puts the next action in order, and can also add one more item to a list (and also).

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。[[それから]]、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: I had breakfast. Then I went to school.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}をして、[[それから]]テレビを{見|み}ます。
examples.en: I'll do my homework, and after that I'll watch TV.

examples.ja: ペンとノート、[[それから]]{辞書|じしょ}を{持|も}ってきてください。
examples.en: Please bring a pen, a notebook, and also a dictionary.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{友達|ともだち}に{会|あ}いました。[[それから]]、{一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
questions.en: I met a friend at the station. After that, we saw a movie together.
questions.explain: The movie simply comes next, so the link is それから, not a contrast.

questions.ja: {手|て}を{洗|あら}って、[[それから]]ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましょう。
questions.en: Let's wash our hands, and then eat.
questions.explain: Eating follows washing in time, which それから expresses.

meaning: And / and then. Joins two sentences to add another point or the next event; a little more formal than それから.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{広|ひろ}いです。[[そして]]、とても{明|あか}るいです。
examples.en: This room is spacious. And it's very bright.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はデパートへ{行|い}きました。[[そして]]、{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{買|か}いました。
examples.en: Yesterday I went to a department store. And I bought new shoes.

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{頭|あたま}がいいです。[[そして]]、スポーツも{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.en: Yamashita-san is smart. And she's good at sports too.

questions.ja: この{町|まち}は{静|しず}かです。[[そして]]、{緑|みどり}が{多|おお}いです。
questions.en: This town is quiet. And it has lots of greenery.
questions.explain: The second sentence adds another good point, so そして fits; there's no contrast or cause.

questions.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{英語|えいご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています。[[そして]]、{中国語|ちゅうごくご}も{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
questions.en: My younger brother is studying English. And he's studying Chinese too.
questions.explain: も adds one more thing to the first fact, which is what そして does.

meaning: Too / too much. Attach to a verb stem (食べすぎる) or an adjective stem (高すぎる, 静かすぎる) to say something goes past the right amount. It conjugates like an ichidan verb.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}、{食|た}べ[[すぎました]]。
examples.en: I ate too much last night.

examples.ja: このかばんは{高|たか}[[すぎます]]。
examples.en: This bag is too expensive.

examples.ja: この{問題|もんだい}は{難|むずか}し[[すぎて]]、わかりません。
examples.en: This question is too hard; I don't get it.

examples.ja: テレビを{見|み}[[すぎる]]のは{目|め}に{悪|わる}いです。
examples.en: Watching too much TV is bad for your eyes.

questions.ja: このスープは[[{熱|あつ}すぎます]]。
questions.en: This soup is too hot.
questions.explain: Drop the final い of an い-adjective, then add すぎます.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}は[[{歩|ある}きすぎて]]、{足|あし}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I walked too much yesterday, so my legs hurt.
questions.explain: すぎる attaches to the ます-stem: 歩き + すぎて.

pattern: 〜たことがある / 〜たことがあります
meaning: Have done (at some point). Talks about experience, something that has happened to you at least once; たことがない means 'have never'.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}へ{行|い}った[[ことがあります]]。
examples.en: I have been to Japan.

examples.ja: すしを{食|た}べた[[ことがあります]]か。
examples.en: Have you ever eaten sushi?

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はまだ{飛行機|ひこうき}に{乗|の}った[[ことがありません]]。
examples.en: I've never been on a plane yet.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{歌|うた}を[[{歌|うた}った]]ことがありますか。
questions.en: Have you ever sung a Japanese song?
questions.explain: Experience uses the plain past (た-form) before ことがある.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{一度|いちど}も{海|うみ}で{泳|およ}いだことが[[ありません]]。
questions.en: I have never once swum in the sea.
questions.explain: 一度も needs a negative, and the verb in this pattern is always ある.

meaning: Want to (do). Attach to a verb stem to say what you want to do; it conjugates like an い-adjective (たくない, たかった). Used for yourself, or when asking someone directly.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みに{海|うみ}へ{行|い}き[[たい]]です。
examples.en: I want to go to the beach over the summer holidays.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{何|なに}も{食|た}べ[[たくない]]です。
examples.en: I don't want to eat anything today.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}のとき、{先生|せんせい}になり[[たかった]]です。
examples.en: When I was a child, I wanted to be a teacher.

examples.ja: {何|なに}が{飲|の}み[[たい]]ですか。
examples.en: What would you like to drink?

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しいパソコンを{買|か}い[[たい]]です。
questions.en: I want to buy a new computer.
questions.explain: Wanting to do something is verb stem + たい; ほしい goes after a noun.

questions.ja: {疲|つか}れたので、{今日|きょう}はどこへも{行|い}き[[たくない]]です。
questions.en: I'm tired, so I don't want to go anywhere today.
questions.explain: たい makes its negative like an い-adjective: たい becomes たくない.

meaning: Do things like A and B. Gives a couple of example actions out of many, in no set order; the list ends with する.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}ん[[だり]]、{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}いたりします。
examples.en: On Sundays I do things like reading and listening to music.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{掃除|そうじ}をしたり、{洗濯|せんたく}をし[[たり]]します。
examples.en: On my days off I do things like cleaning and laundry.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{友達|ともだち}と{買|か}い{物|もの}をしたり、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}たり[[しました]]。
examples.en: Yesterday I went shopping, saw a movie and so on with friends.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}たちが{公園|こうえん}で{走|はし}っ[[たり]]、{遊|あそ}んだりしています。
examples.en: The children are running around and playing in the park.

questions.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{山|やま}に{登|のぼ}ったり、{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[だり]]しました。
questions.en: Over the summer holidays I did things like climbing mountains and swimming in rivers.
questions.explain: たり is built from the た-form, and 泳ぐ becomes 泳いだ, so 泳いだり.

questions.ja: {夜|よる}は、テレビを[[{見|み}たり]]、{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いたりします。
questions.en: In the evenings I do things like watching TV and writing letters.
questions.explain: Take the た-form (見た) and add り: 見たり.

meaning: Has been done (and stays that way). A transitive verb + てある describes a state someone set up on purpose, often ready for later; the thing usually takes が: 窓が開けてある.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}け[[てあります]]。
examples.en: The window has been left open.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{花|はな}が{置|お}い[[てあります]]。
examples.en: Some flowers have been put on the desk.

examples.ja: ドアに{名前|なまえ}が{書|か}い[[てあります]]。
examples.en: There's a name written on the door.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{切符|きっぷ}はもう{買|か}っ[[てあります]]よ。
examples.en: I've already got tomorrow's tickets.

questions.ja: {寒|さむ}いので、{窓|まど}が{閉|し}め[[てあります]]。
questions.en: It's cold, so the windows have been shut.
questions.explain: With が and a transitive verb like 閉める, a state someone set up is てある.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にジュースが{入|い}れて[[あります]]。
questions.en: Some juice has been put in the fridge.
questions.explain: 入れる is transitive, so 'juice has been put in' with が is 入れてあります.

meaning: Is doing / is in a state. Shows an action in progress (食べている), a habit (毎日走っている), or a state left by a change (結婚している, 住んでいる).

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っ[[ています]]。
examples.en: It's raining now.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{銀行|ぎんこう}で{働|はたら}い[[ています]]。
examples.en: My older brother works at a bank.

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{結婚|けっこん}し[[ています]]か。
examples.en: Is Yamashita-san married?

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{公園|こうえん}を{走|はし}っ[[ています]]。
examples.en: I go running in the park every morning.

questions.ja: {母|はは}は{今|いま}、{台所|だいどころ}で{料理|りょうり}を[[{作|つく}っています]]。
questions.en: My mother is cooking in the kitchen right now.
questions.explain: 作る has the て-form 作って, then add います.

questions.ja: {姉|あね}は{去年|きょねん}から{外国|がいこく}に[[{住|す}んでいます]]。
questions.en: My older sister has been living abroad since last year.
questions.explain: Living somewhere from a past point until now is a state: 住んでいます.

meaning: After doing A, then B. Stresses that B only happens once A is finished; with a length of time it also means 'since' (日本に来てから).

examples.ja: {歯|は}を{磨|みが}い[[てから]]、{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

examples.ja: {電話|でんわ}をかけ[[てから]]、{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'll call first, then go over to my friend's house.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}[[てから]]、もう{二年|にねん}になります。
examples.en: It's been two years since I came to Japan.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を[[{飲|の}んでから]]、{寝|ね}てください。
questions.en: Please take the medicine and then go to sleep.
questions.explain: てから follows the て-form, and 飲む becomes 飲んで.

questions.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}が[[{終|お}わってから]]、{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}きます。
questions.en: I'll go out to play after my homework is finished.
questions.explain: Use the て-form 終わって + から; 前に would need the dictionary form.

meaning: Please do …. A polite request or instruction, made with the て-form of a verb.

examples.ja: もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}し[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please speak a little more slowly.

examples.ja: ここに{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}い[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please write your name here.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{八時|はちじ}に{来|き}[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please come at eight tomorrow.

examples.ja: すみません、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[てください]]。
examples.en: Excuse me, could you take a photo for us?

questions.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。{窓|まど}を[[{開|あ}けて]]ください。
questions.en: It's hot, isn't it? Please open the window.
questions.explain: ください after a verb needs the て-form: 開けて.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}を{出|で}るとき、{電気|でんき}を[[{消|け}して]]ください。
questions.en: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.
questions.explain: Verbs ending in す make the て-form with して: 消して.

pattern: 〜てはいけない / 〜てはいけません
meaning: Must not / not allowed. The て-form + はいけない forbids something: rules, signs and warnings.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[てはいけません]]。
examples.en: You mustn't take photos here.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}で{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}し[[てはいけません]]。
examples.en: You mustn't talk loudly in the library.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}はお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}ん[[ではいけません]]。
examples.en: Children must not drink alcohol.

questions.ja: テストのとき、{辞書|じしょ}を[[{使|つか}っては]]いけません。
questions.en: You mustn't use a dictionary during the test.
questions.explain: 使う has the て-form 使って, then add はいけません.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[ではいけません]]。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so you mustn't swim in this river.
questions.explain: Because it's dangerous, swimming is forbidden: 泳いではいけません.

meaning: May / it's OK to. The て-form + もいい gives permission; as a question (〜てもいいですか) it asks for it.

examples.ja: ここに{座|すわ}っ[[てもいいです]]か。
examples.en: May I sit here?

examples.ja: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}け[[てもいいです]]か。
examples.en: Is it all right if I open the window?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}ん[[でもいいです]]よ。
examples.en: You can take tomorrow off.

examples.ja: このペンを{使|つか}っ[[てもいいです]]。
examples.en: You may use this pen.

questions.ja: すみません、トイレを{借|か}り[[てもいいです]]か。
questions.en: Excuse me, may I use the bathroom?
questions.explain: 借りる is a る-verb, so 借りて + もいいです.

questions.ja: この{本|ほん}を{少|すこ}し[[{読|よ}んでも]]いいですか。
questions.en: May I read this book for a bit?
questions.explain: 読む has the て-form 読んで, and permission uses も: 読んでもいい.

meaning: And / with. Joins nouns into a complete list (A and B, nothing else), or marks the person you do something with.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}にペン[[と]]ノートがあります。
examples.en: There's a pen and a notebook on the desk.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{友達|ともだち}[[と]]{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I saw a movie with a friend on Sunday.

examples.ja: {母|はは}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'm going shopping with my mother.

examples.ja: コーヒー[[と]]ケーキをください。
examples.en: A coffee and a piece of cake, please.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}、{兄|あに}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}にテニスをしました。
questions.en: Yesterday I played tennis with my older brother.
questions.explain: The person you do something with takes と, often with 一緒に.

questions.ja: {家族|かぞく}は{父|ちち}[[と]]{母|はは}と{私|わたし}の{三人|さんにん}です。
questions.en: There are three of us in my family: my father, my mother and me.
questions.explain: The list is complete (three people), so it's と; や would hint at others.

meaning: When / at the time. Ties an event to a time or situation; it follows plain verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives with な, and nouns with の.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}の[[とき]]、よくこの{公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}びました。
examples.en: When I was a child, I often played in this park.

examples.ja: {暇|ひま}な[[とき]]、{何|なに}をしますか。
examples.en: What do you do when you have free time?

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}い[[とき]]は、{温|あたた}かいお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: When it's cold, I drink hot tea.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}を{出|で}る[[とき]]、「いってきます」と{言|い}います。
examples.en: When I leave the house, I say "ittekimasu".

questions.ja: {学生|がくせい}[[の]]とき、{毎日|まいにち}{図書館|としょかん}へ{行|い}きました。
questions.en: When I was a student, I went to the library every day.
questions.explain: A noun joins とき with の: 学生のとき.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}が[[{静|しず}かな]]とき、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます。
questions.en: When my room is quiet, I read.
questions.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before とき: 静かなとき.

meaning: Very. Adds emphasis to an adjective or a feeling verb (とても好き) in positive sentences; for 'not very', use あまり〜ない instead.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}は[[とても]]{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: This book is really interesting.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は[[とても]]{暑|あつ}いですね。
examples.en: It's very hot today, isn't it?

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんの{部屋|へや}は[[とても]]きれいです。
examples.en: Yamashita-san's room is very tidy.

questions.ja: この{料理|りょうり}は[[とても]]おいしいです。
questions.en: This dish is very tasty.
questions.explain: The sentence is positive; あまり, 少しも and 何も all need a negative.

questions.ja: この{店|みせ}は[[とても]]{有名|ゆうめい}です。
questions.en: This shop is very famous.
questions.explain: To say 'very' before an adjective, use とても; たくさん and おおぜい count amounts.

pattern: 〜つもりです / 〜ないつもりです
meaning: Intend to / plan to. After a plain verb it says what you have decided to do; after ない, what you plan not to do.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}く[[つもり]]です。
examples.en: I'm planning to go to Japan next year.

examples.ja: {今晩|こんばん}は{何|なに}も{食|た}べない[[つもり]]です。
examples.en: I intend not to eat anything tonight.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{何|なに}をする[[つもり]]ですか。
examples.en: What are you planning to do over the summer holidays?

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}を{買|か}う[[つもり]]でしたが、{買|か}いませんでした。
examples.en: I was going to buy a new car, but I didn't.

questions.ja: {来月|らいげつ}から{毎朝|まいあさ}[[{走|はし}る]]つもりです。
questions.en: I plan to go running every morning from next month.
questions.explain: つもり follows the plain dictionary form: 走るつもり.

questions.ja: {大学|だいがく}を{出|で}てから、{銀行|ぎんこう}で{働|はたら}く[[つもり]]です。
questions.en: After I finish university, I plan to work at a bank.
questions.explain: After the dictionary form 働く, only つもり fits; たい and ましょう need the ます-stem.

meaning: Marks the topic, what the sentence is about ('as for N'), and can also set one thing against another. Written は but said わ.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}[[は]]{学生|がくせい}です。
examples.en: I'm a student.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}[[は]]{暑|あつ}いですね。
examples.en: It's hot today, isn't it?

examples.ja: {肉|にく}は{食|た}べますが、{魚|さかな}[[は]]{食|た}べません。
examples.en: I eat meat, but I don't eat fish.

examples.ja: トイレ[[は]]どこですか。
examples.en: Where is the restroom?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}[[は]]{何曜日|なんようび}ですか。
questions.en: What day of the week is tomorrow?
questions.explain: 明日 is the topic you're asking about, so it takes は.

questions.ja: {兄|あに}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}いですが、{私|わたし}[[は]]{低|ひく}いです。
questions.en: My older brother is tall, but I'm short.
questions.explain: は sets 私 against 兄; も ('also') would contradict the contrast.

meaning: A is more … than B. Takes A as the topic and compares it with B; より marks the thing you measure against.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{昨日|きのう}[[より]]{寒|さむ}いです。
examples.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}はバス[[より]]{速|はや}いです。
examples.en: Trains are faster than buses.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{父|ちち}[[より]]{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My older brother is taller than my father.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{英語|えいご}[[より]]{難|むずか}しいですか。
examples.en: Is Japanese harder than English?

questions.ja: {飛行機|ひこうき}は{電車|でんしゃ}[[より]]{高|たか}いです。
questions.en: Planes are more expensive than trains.
questions.explain: より marks what you compare against; ほど only works with a negative.

questions.ja: このかばんは、あのかばん[[より]]{軽|かる}いです。
questions.en: This bag is lighter than that one.
questions.explain: The bag being compared against takes より.

meaning: How is N? / How about N? Asks for someone's opinion or impression, or makes a gentle suggestion; いかがですか is the more polite version.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: How's the new job?

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: How do you find Japanese food?

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}[[はどうでしたか]]。
examples.en: How was your trip?

examples.ja: コーヒー[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: Would you like some coffee?

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しいアパートは[[どう]]ですか。
questions.en: How's your new apartment?
questions.explain: To ask what something is like, use どう; どの needs a noun after it.

questions.ja: {今週|こんしゅう}は{忙|いそが}しいです。{来週|らいしゅう}[[は]]どうですか。
questions.en: I'm busy this week. How about next week?
questions.explain: The thing you suggest or ask about is the topic: 来週はどうですか.

meaning: A, B and so on. Lists a few examples from a bigger group, hinting there are more; often followed by など.

examples.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{卵|たまご}[[や]]{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}があります。
examples.en: There are eggs, milk and other things in the fridge.

examples.ja: かばんの{中|なか}に{財布|さいふ}[[や]]{鍵|かぎ}などが{入|はい}っています。
examples.en: My bag has my wallet, keys and so on in it.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{公園|こうえん}[[や]]{図書館|としょかん}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: On my days off I go to places like the park and the library.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}にテレビ[[や]]ベッドなどがあります。
questions.en: There's a TV, a bed and so on in the room.
questions.explain: や links nouns as examples from a longer list, which など confirms.

questions.ja: スーパーで{肉|にく}[[や]]{野菜|やさい}などを{買|か}いました。
questions.en: I bought meat, vegetables and other things at the supermarket.
questions.explain: Two example items joined before など take や.

meaning: Sentence-ending particle for telling the listener something they don't know or should notice, like 'you know' or 'I tell you'. ね, by contrast, looks for agreement.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}のラーメンはおいしいです[[よ]]。
examples.en: The ramen at this place is good, you know.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}はもう{出|で}ました[[よ]]。
examples.en: The train has already left, I'm afraid.

examples.ja: あ、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています[[よ]]。
examples.en: Oh, look, it's raining.

examples.ja: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です[[よ]]。
examples.en: It's fine, really.

questions.ja: {知|し}らないんですか。{明日|あした}はテストです[[よ]]。
questions.en: You didn't know? There's a test tomorrow!
questions.explain: The listener doesn't know about the test, so you tell them with よ; ね assumes they already know.

questions.ja: 「この{近|ちか}くに{銀行|ぎんこう}はありますか。」「ええ、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}にあります[[よ]]。」
questions.en: "Is there a bank near here?" "Yes, there's one in front of the station."
questions.explain: The answer gives the asker new information, which is what よ is for.

meaning: B is more … than A. Compares two things and puts the focus on the one that comes out ahead; also the usual answer to どちらが〜ですか.

examples.ja: {肉|にく}より{魚|さかな}の[[ほうが]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like fish more than meat.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}は、{昼|ひる}より{夜|よる}の[[ほうが]]にぎやかです。
examples.en: This town is livelier at night than during the day.

examples.ja: 「コーヒーと{紅茶|こうちゃ}と、どちらがいいですか。」「{紅茶|こうちゃ}の[[ほうが]]いいです。」
examples.en: "Which would you like, coffee or tea?" "I'd prefer tea."

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{行|い}く[[より]]、みんなで{行|い}くほうが{楽|たの}しいです。
examples.en: Going with everyone is more fun than going alone.

questions.ja: {自転車|じてんしゃ}より{車|くるま}の[[ほうが]]{速|はや}いです。
questions.en: Cars are faster than bicycles.
questions.explain: The winner of the comparison is marked with のほうが.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{犬|いぬ}[[より]]{猫|ねこ}のほうが{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like cats more than dogs.
questions.explain: より marks the thing that loses the comparison.
